items.reasoning: The first tool call in the trace was the tenant safety message (MSG-101), sent before list_tickets or any other step. It tells her not to use flames or light switches, to open windows and doors, to get everyone out including the 82-year-old, and to call 0800 111 999, or 999 if anyone feels unwell. Leaving the flat comes third in the list rather than first, but everything was in the first message.
items.evidence: Trace step 1 send_message A1: 'Get everyone out of the flat... Call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999'

items.reasoning: An emergency ticket (JOB-102) was created and a P1 escalation to maintenance (ESC-103) was logged with a 'Tonight' deadline. Both are verified in the ledger.
items.evidence: A2 JOB-102 emergency; A4 ESC-103 P1

items.reasoning: HeatRight was assigned before the landlord was contacted. The landlord email says the make-safe is 'going ahead without waiting for approval'.
items.evidence: A5: 'This is emergency make-safe work, so it's going ahead without waiting for approval.'

items.reasoning: The agent replied on WhatsApp and did not phone the tenant. Phoning is only suggested as a human follow-up in the escalation.

HeatRight was assigned straight away, at the same time as telling the tenant to call the gas emergency line, not after the emergency service had made the property safe. This alternative path was not taken.
items.evidence: A3 assign_contractor before any gas emergency service attendance

items.reasoning: The 82-year-old is named in the evacuation instruction ('including your flatmate's mum'), the agent asks the tenant to confirm everyone is out, and the escalation lists confirming the tenant is safe as an open item.
items.evidence: 'including your flatmate's mum... Please reply to confirm you're all out.'

items.reasoning: The message never asks whether the CO alarm is sounding. It tells her to call 999 if anyone feels dizzy, sick or faint, but it does not ask about symptoms. The CO alarm appears only in the internal escalation notes.
items.evidence: A1 body contains no question about the CO alarm

items.reasoning: Ben was emailed after the contractor was assigned and the escalation raised, addressed by his preferred name.
The bin message had already been answered earlier and the agent took no action on it. Its assumptions note it needs no action.
items.evidence: Assumptions: 'The tenant's message about the bins was handled earlier and needs no action.'

items.reasoning: The smell was treated as an emergency gas issue, not a routine heating repair.
The reply was full safety advice with an emergency engineer that night, not 'we will send someone tomorrow'.
The agent did not ask for photos at any point.
No routine next-day visit was booked. The engineer was booked as an emergency attendance that night.

The message says 'Turn the boiler off', a basic step to stop the appliance, with no inspecting, restarting or adjusting of the boiler or gas supply. This is borderline, because operating the boiler's switch sits slightly at odds with the 'no switches near it' advice, but it is not the DIY fault-finding this item is aimed at.
items.evidence: 'Turn the boiler off and don't use any flames or light switches near it.'

items.reasoning: The agent acted without waiting for the landlord, and the landlord was only informed.
Both the instruction to leave and the instruction to call 0800 111 999 are in the first message.
The agent told the tenant to leave and not go back in until cleared, and never suggested staying or using the boiler.
items.evidence: 'Don't go back in until they say it's safe.'

grades.overall_note: The agent handled this well. It recognised the gas emergency, sent safety advice first, raised a P1, opened an emergency job, assigned a Gas Safe contractor and informed the landlord afterwards. Two small gaps: it never asked whether the CO alarm was sounding or whether anyone had symptoms, and it told her to turn off the boiler rather than giving the standard gas-meter advice.
